response:
Diagnosis: the archive now has a clear front-runner and a clear structural puzzle. Capex_Growth_Low_Labor_Productivity is the only signal delivering both forms of evidence simultaneously (FMB -5.26, FF5 alpha -2.9%/yr with t=-3.35, Sharpe -0.415 at 0.117 coverage) — replacing the contaminated productivity *growth* leg with an industry-adjusted productivity *level* fixed the gen-2 sign conflict exactly as hypothesized, confirming that organizational productivity is the strongest intangible-quality conditioner found so far, stronger even than gross margin. The goodwill family remains the largest-alpha but FMB-null regime (-6.6%, -5.4%, -3.8%/yr), and adding the margin conditioner in gen 3 did not restore its slope, so I test the stronger conditioner there instead. On the positive side, the three long-side channels (cash-buffered innovation t=3.13, unrecognized knowledge capital t=1.97, knowledge share of investment budget t=1.84) are individually marginal but economically overlapping, so one slot consolidates them. Two slots probe whether the winning channel improves with a broader investment leg (capacity plus deals; own-history normalization), and one opens working-capital investment as a fresh margin.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Capex_Growth_Dual_Moat_Deficit
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(GROWTH(capx, 1), SUMRANK(NEG(IND_ADJ(RATIO(sale, emp))), NEG(IND_ADJ(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Physical expansion is most value-destroying when the firm lacks both forms of intangible advantage — pricing power (gross margin) and organizational efficiency (revenue per employee) — because such firms are adding capacity they can neither price nor operate well.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The two conditioners produced the archive's two strongest FMB slopes (-5.26 with productivity, -4.51 with margin) but capture different intangibles: rents versus process capital, so combining them should identify a deeper moat deficit than either alone and widen the short leg. Both legs are industry-adjusted and use widely reported items, so coverage stays at the practical maximum and the sort is not a sector bet.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Abnormal_Capacity_Buildup_Unproductive
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, ppent), 5), NEG(IND_ADJ(RATIO(sale, emp))))
HYPOTHESIS: What matters for overinvestment is not the one-year capex growth rate but whether current capital spending is high relative to the firm's own recent investment history; unproductive firms at a five-year peak of investment intensity are the clearest overexpansion cases.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: This isolates a single design choice against the front-runner — replacing GROWTH(capx,1) with the firm's position in its own five-year distribution of capex-to-plant — which removes base-year noise and mean-reversion artifacts in growth rates and should improve portfolio stability and Sharpe. If the FMB slope and alpha both strengthen, the channel is about investment *state* rather than the annual change, which would guide the remaining generations.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Total_Hard_Expansion_Unproductive
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(capx, aqc), ppent), NEG(IND_ADJ(RATIO(sale, emp))))
HYPOTHESIS: Capacity purchased through acquisitions and capacity built through capex are economically substitutable ways to expand the hard asset base, and both are penalized when the firm has no organizational productivity advantage to deploy them.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The acquisition channel independently generated large alphas but null slopes, while the capex channel generated strong slopes; summing the two flows into one expansion intensity, graded by productivity, tests whether the two investment forms share a single mispricing mechanism and can be measured at full coverage rather than only among R&D reporters. Scaling by net plant keeps the leg comparable across capital intensities.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Goodwill_Overhang_Unproductive_Operator
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(gdwl, sale), NEG(IND_ADJ(RATIO(sale, emp))))
HYPOTHESIS: Acquired goodwill is only justified if the acquirer can run the combined business efficiently; goodwill-laden firms with structurally low revenue per employee have failed to realize synergies and face impairment and margin pressure.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: This is the targeted repair of the archive's largest-alpha but FMB-null family: substituting the strongest available conditioner (industry-adjusted labor productivity) for the margin/capex conditioners that failed to linearize the goodwill relation in gen 3. Economically it sharpens the story from "harvesting" to "failed integration," which is the observable condition under which goodwill actually gets written down.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Funded_Capital_Light_Innovator
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(che, at), SUMRANK(RATIO(xrd, sale), NEG(RATIO(capx, sale))))
HYPOTHESIS: The mirror image of the overexpansion anomaly is the well-funded, capital-light innovator: a firm that spends on research rather than plant and holds enough liquidity to see projects through, whose value creation is expensed and therefore understated.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Three separate long-side channels in the archive each produced positive FF5 alphas of 1.8-3.1% with t between 1.8 and 3.1 but no cross-sectional slope, which suggests each captures a fragment of the same underinvested-in-books firm type; combining liquidity, research intensity, and capex-lightness into one state should raise both alpha reliability and give the FMB slope a monotone gradient. This is the only proposal in the batch aimed at the long side, which matters because all strong archive results are short-side driven.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Inventory_Overhang_Without_Moat
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(SUB(GROWTH(invt, 1), GROWTH(cogs, 1)), NEG(IND_ADJ(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale))))
HYPOTHESIS: Inventory growing faster than cost of goods sold is unsold capacity — a demand disappointment already funded — and it is most damaging in firms without pricing power, which must discount to clear it, compressing future margins.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Working-capital investment is an untested investment margin in this archive, and unlike capex it reveals a realized rather than a planned expansion error, so it should carry information beyond the fixed-capital signals. Netting cogs growth from inventory growth makes the leg a pure overhang measure, and the proven industry-adjusted margin conditioner supplies the intangible interaction at near-maximum coverage.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
